differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Models optimized for writes and reads are distinct.
differences.rightDesc: Single model handles all data operations.

differences.title: 2. PERFORMANCE
differences.leftDesc: Optimized paths for queries and commands enhance performance.
differences.rightDesc: Performance can be limited by unified operations.

differences.title: 3. COMPLEXITY
differences.leftDesc: Requires more effort to set up and manage distinct models.
differences.rightDesc: Easier to understand and implement initially.

differences.title: 4. READ OPTIMIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Read models can be denormalized for faster queries.
differences.rightDesc: Reads are performed on the primary data store.

differences.title: 5. WRITE OPTIMIZATION
differences.leftDesc: Command side handles complex business logic efficiently.

differences.title: 6. EVENTUAL CONSISTENCY
differences.leftDesc: Read models may lag slightly behind write operations.
differences.rightDesc: Writes are usually reflected immediately in reads.

differences.title: 7. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for systems with heavy read/write separation needs.
differences.rightDesc: Suitable for basic data management tasks.
